I wake before the city wakes and breathe slowly early
The kitchen holds a quiet patient blue light and silence
Coffee steams in the mug near the open door softly
Bread crumbles under my fingers and a little salt again
The radio murmurs an old song I know well again
A cup cools on the windowsill outside the room brightly
I read the notes left by my patient hands again
The notebook opens to a page of gray rain softly
I write down one small ordinary thing each morning again
The day begins as a door opens softly into light

Outside buses pass in long silver lines along the street
People walk with heads bent to glowing phones and hurry
A child laughs near a bakery window full of warmth
Vendors call their prices before the sun climbs slowly above
A bird perches on a tangled black wire above here
The street smells of rain and old metal and dust
A man checks a paper map with quiet care again
The crosswalk light blinks red and patient again and again
I buy a banana and a small bright dream here
The city exhales and I keep walking through the streets

Memory arrives without knocking soft as warm morning steam still
A summer kitchen fills with lemon light and heat again
The voice of my grandmother says please walk slowly here
We ate sweet melon in the wide yellow yard then
Mosquitoes tapped the screen in tiny patient code all night
Water droplets rolled across a paper bag with soft sound
I remember the sound of the old stone well clear
The bucket lowered down with creak and quiet trust again
Dust moved in the beam like gold fish swimming slowly
Time stopped for a small and shining quiet moment now

A song plays in my skull now and always still
The melody changes shape when I think about it again
I cannot keep it inside my open patient hands again
It slips through fingers like a small green bird away
I let it go before it breaks into silence again
Yet the memory remains a warm glowing ember now here
I carry it through ordinary streets and quiet rooms again
A small bright drawing sticks to the cold fridge now
The colors are yellow blue and red and green bright
A small face peeks out smiling without words ever here

I write because silence grows too heavy for me now
The pen rests then moves across a blank page slowly
Words choose each other like small quiet friends around fire
One word refuses stubbornly as if it were a stone
I circle it, cross it out, and begin again slowly
The notebook asks a question with no name at all
I answer in small fragments of light and dust now
A sentence opens like a door in the fog outside
I step through it into another quiet thought room now
The page holds all that I can bear now here

At night the phone becomes a small pale moon above
Notifications arrive like small birds tapping at the glass softly
I scroll but the world does not blink once now
A message appears asking are you sleeping or lost tonight
I do not reply at once not yet tonight here
Instead I watch my own pale reflection on the screen
The room tilts into a dark blue cave around me
Stars are absent outside but I imagine them above still
My breath makes a small cloud in the dark again
I set the phone face down on the pillow softly

Sleep arrives like a tide rolling from the sea slowly
I am tired in a strange soft tired way now
The ceiling becomes a night sky then slowly forgets me
I float somewhere between thought and no thought at all
A dream starts with a yellow field at noon here
Wind walks through the grass naming nothing in particular now
I am a person without a name for a while
A river runs through the dream with soft silver music
The fish swim upward looking for a blue sky again
I try to swim but the water is light only

Something whispers softly that you may rest here now safe
The name that matters returns for a short moment now
A doorway appears in the edge of the sleep now
I step toward it one step no more perhaps yet
The door is not a door but a sound old
It hums the old song from a distant kitchen again
I close my eyes and let the song hold me
When I open my eyes the room is small now
The clock says it is morning but I hesitate again
I sit up slowly with dust and old memory near

The floor feels cool beneath my bare feet once again
Sunlight has moved across the blanket by this morning now
I stretch my hands toward the bright quiet window now
The world is ordinary now and that is enough again
I notice the cat blinking slowly by the table now
Its eyes are amber quiet and kind in the light
I make tea because my restless hands need work now
The kettle sings a sharp brief song then stops again
I pour the water and watch the leaves unfold slowly
Each cup is a small quiet pause in time now

I write another line then another line then more words
The words are not answers but small footsteps now here
They move through me and change the shape of day
I think freedom is a practice not a place now
I think attention is a gift I can keep giving
I think joy is a door I must walk through
I think rest is not laziness but care and work
The sentence becomes a path and the path a map
I am the writer and I am also the reader
So the writing remains ordinary warm and alive to me
